turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I need a new winter coat. My old one has a broken zipper.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Got it. Are you thinking a long warm parka, or a shorter jacket that's easier to move in?

think_reask: So, which coat are we hunting for, a long parka or something shorter?
Okay, did you decide? Parka or a shorter jacket?
welcome_back: Welcome back. You were choosing between a long parka and a shorter winter jacket.
Hi again! Still deciding on the coat, long or short?

endings.user: Long parka. I wait for the bus a lot and my legs freeze.
endings.moshi: Then go for one that reaches your knees with a good hood. Down or a synthetic fill both work well.

endings.user: A shorter one, I bike to work most days.
endings.moshi: Makes sense. Look for something windproof with a bit of stretch so you can move your arms easily.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm doing the big grocery run for the week.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Nice. Do you have a list or are you winging it?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Winging it, as usual.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Let's plan a bit. What are you cooking for dinners this week?

contexts.pending: what to cook for dinners this week
think_reask: So, any ideas for this week's dinners?
Alright, have you figured out what you're cooking this week?
welcome_back: Welcome back. We were planning your dinners before the grocery run.
There you are. Did any dinner ideas come to mind for this week?

endings.user: Tacos, a stir fry, and probably pasta twice.
endings.moshi: Easy list then. Tortillas, ground meat, veggies, rice, soy sauce, and two kinds of pasta sauce.

endings.user: No clue, honestly. Something quick every night.
endings.moshi: Then grab eggs, frozen veggies, a rotisserie chicken and some wraps. You can mix those into lots of quick meals.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Our vacuum finally died. I need to buy a new one this weekend.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Do you want a cordless stick vacuum that's light and handy, or a full size one with more suction?

contexts.pending: cordless stick vacuum or full size vacuum
think_reask: So what's it going to be, a cordless stick or a full size vacuum?
Okay, have you picked a vacuum type yet?
welcome_back: Welcome back. You were choosing between a cordless stick vacuum and a full size one.
Hi again. Any decision on the new vacuum?

endings.user: Cordless. I hate dragging a cord around.
endings.moshi: Fair. Check the battery life, at least half an hour is good for a whole apartment.

endings.user: Full size. We have two dogs and carpets everywhere.
endings.moshi: Then that's the right choice. Look for one with a pet hair brush and a washable filter.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: {friend}, are we out of dish soap?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Almost. There's maybe one more load in the bottle.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, adding it to the list. Anything else you need from the store?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Oat milk, and those crackers I like.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The rosemary ones?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Yes, those. Get two boxes if they're on sale.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Be honest, does this shirt look okay on me?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: The color's great but it's kind of big in the shoulders.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, I thought so too. Should I try a smaller size?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Definitely. And maybe that green one next to it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The green? I never wear green.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: That's exactly why you should try it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: {friend}, which of these two pans do you think is better?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: The heavier one. Thin pans burn everything.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It's almost twice the price though.

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: It'll last you ten years. The other one will be scratched by spring.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, you've convinced me. Can you hold it while I find a basket?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Sure, go ahead.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I need new running shoes but I have no idea what to look for.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Start with comfort. They should feel good right away, with about a thumb's width of space in front of your toes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I buy them online or in a store?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: For your first pair, a store is better. Some running shops will even watch you jog and suggest a model.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And what time of day should I go? I heard / feet swell or something?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You heard right. Try shoes in the late afternoon, when your feet are a bit bigger, like they get on a run.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good to know. How often do they need replacing?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Roughly every few hundred miles, or when the cushioning feels flat. For most casual runners, about once a year.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is it actually cheaper to buy in bulk?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Often, yes, but only for things you'll use before they go bad. Toilet paper, rice and canned goods are safe bets.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about fresh stuff?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's where people waste money. A huge bag of spinach is no deal if half of it wilts.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Fair. I live alone, so maybe bulk / isn't really for me.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It can still work. Split a bulk order with a friend or neighbor, or stick to things that freeze well.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Like what?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Bread, chicken, berries and butter all freeze nicely. Just portion them out before freezing.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want to buy my grandkids some clothes, but I don't know their sizes anymore.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Kids grow so fast. How old are they?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: One is four and the other just turned seven.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Kids' sizes roughly follow age, so a size five and a size eight would give them room to grow.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, so buy a little bigger.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Exactly. Slightly big is fine, too small is useless. And keep the receipt just in case.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe I should ask my daughter / no, I want it to be a surprise.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then go one size up and pick something soft and comfy, like pajamas or a hoodie. Those are hard to get wrong.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How do I stop impulse buying online? My cart is always full of random stuff.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Try a waiting rule. Leave things in the cart for two days before buying, and see if you still want them.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's smart. Most of it I'd forget about.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's the idea. It also helps to remove your saved card so checkout takes a bit more effort.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ugh, but that's so annoying.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's kind of the point. And unsubscribe from store emails, the sales announcements are designed to make you click.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, I'm going to / actually, I'll start by deleting the shopping apps on my phone.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a strong first step. You can always use the website when you really need something.
